chapter_title: AI Agents, Prompts, and Rubric Scoring
learning_objective: The learner will classify each of eight tasks as one an assistant can do in a single reply or one that needs an agent working in several steps, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** assistant-or-agent-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of eight tasks as one an assistant can do in a single reply or one that needs an agent working in several steps, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** AI Assistant, Large Language Model, AI Agent (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each task the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) An agent is just a better assistant. (2) Any task with several sentences needs an agent. (3) An assistant can run a link checker by itself. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying a task by whether it needs steps and tools is an Understand-level action that guides the learner's choice of tool. Four tasks per bin teach the learner to look for steps, tools, and files. **Content:** The two bins: Assistant (one reply from the model is enough) and Agent (the task needs several steps, tools, or files). The eight tasks: | # | Task shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Explain what a watershed is in two sentences. | Assistant | One reply can do it. | | 2 | Read every file in this folder, run a link checker on each page, and fill in the rubric worksheet. | Agent | It needs files, a tool, and many steps. | | 3 | Suggest a better title for this lesson. | Assistant | One reply can do it. | | 4 | Open the resource, measure the reading level of three passages with a tool, and report the grade levels. | Agent | It needs a tool and a sequence of steps. | | 5 | Rewrite this paragraph in plain language. | Assistant | One reply can do it. | | 6 | Check all 14 links, record which return errors, and save the list to a file. | Agent | It needs a tool, a record of results, and a file. | | 7 | What does CC BY-SA allow? | Assistant | One reply can do it. | | 8 | Score each of 30 resources against the rubric and save a report for each. | Agent | It needs files, many steps, and repeated work. | **Provenance:** The tasks are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The definitions follow the chapter sections "AI Assistant" and "AI Agent". **Rules:** Each task has exactly one correct bin, four per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one task and the two bins. 2. The learner places the task in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After task 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 tasks in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This needs [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can tell a reply from a job." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed task. **Starting State:** The first task and two empty bins. The question shown is "Is one reply enough, or does this need steps and tools?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says an assistant answers and waits, and an agent plans, acts, observes, and acts again, using tools and files.
